recipes.name: Sundae-bokkeum (Spicy stir-fried blood sausage) 순대볶음
ingredients: 1 pound frozen sundae (Korean blood sausage), thawed
3 ounces of flat starch noodles (or thin dangmyeon), soaked in cold water for an hour
4 ounces of cabbage, sliced into bite-size pieces
8 to 10 large perilla leaves (kkaennip), half of them sliced into bite-size pieces, and half cut into threads
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil (or any cooking oil)
1 tablespoon toasted perilla seeds powder (or toasted sesame seeds powder)
2 tablespoons rice syrup (or sugar to taste)
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the full sealed package of sundae to the boiling water. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 10 minutes. Remove from the pot and transfer to a cutting board to cool down. Drain the noodles and cut them in half. Set aside. Using kitchen scissors, carefully open the package of sundae, then slice them into approximately ¾-inch thick pieces using a sharp kitchen knife. Wipe off the blade of the knife with a wet kitchen towel or paper towel to prevent sticking and ensure a clean cut. Be careful not to break the sundae!
In a bowl, combine gochujang, gochu-garu, soy sauce, rice syrup, and black pepper. Mix well, then add water and stir until thoroughly combined.

Heat the oil in a large pan. Add the minced garlic and stir for about a minute until it becomes slightly crispy. Add the cabbage and stir for 1 minute until it softens slightly. Add onion, green onion, and green chili pepper, stirring with a wooden spoon for about 2 minutes. Add the seasoning sauce, noodles, and half of the sliced perilla leaves. Gently stir for a few minutes until the noodles become soft, shiny, and transparent. Add the sliced sundae and reduce the heat to medium. Gently stir to ensure they are evenly coated with the seasoning. Be careful not to break them open, they are fragile!
Transfer to a plate and garnish with the remaining perilla threads. Sprinkle toasted perilla seeds powder (or toasted sesame seeds powder) on top of the perilla leaves. Serve right away!

instruction_sections.text: Directions
Prepare the sundae and noodles:
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the full sealed package of sundae to the boiling water.
Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 10 minutes.
Remove the sundae package from the pot and put it on a cutting board to cool down.
Drain the noodles and cut them in half. Set aside.

Using kitchen scissors, carefully open the package of sundae, then slice them into approximately ¾-inch thick pieces using a sharp kitchen knife. Wipe off the blade of the knife with a wet kitchen towel or paper towel to prevent sticking and ensure a clean cut. Be careful not to break the sundae!
Prepare the seasoning sauce:
In a bowl, combine gochujang, gochu-garu, soy sauce, rice syrup, and black pepper. Mix well, then add water and stir until thoroughly combined.
Stir fry:
Heat the oil in a large pan. Add the minced garlic and stir for about a minute until it becomes slightly crispy.
Add the cabbage and stir for 1 minute until it softens slightly.
Add onion, green onion, and green chili pepper, stirring with a wooden spoon for about 2 minutes.
Add the seasoning sauce, noodles, and half of the sliced perilla leaves. Gently stir for a few minutes until the noodles become soft, shiny, and transparent.
Add the sliced sundae and reduce the heat to medium. Gently stir to ensure they are evenly coated with the seasoning. Be careful not to break them open, they are fragile!
Serve and enjoy:
Transfer to a plate and garnish with the remaining perilla threads.
Sprinkle toasted perilla seeds powder (or toasted sesame seeds powder) on top of the perilla leaves.
Serve right away!
Put some sundae along with vegetables on an individual plate. Add a little bit of the mixture of perilla leaf threads and perilla seeds powder and enjoy!
